original_question: Let X be a separable Banach space that is weakly sequentially complete. Must X have property (K), meaning that every weak*-null sequence in X* has a convex block subsequence converging to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X)?
target_in_paper: Problem 1.9 in §1.3 (“w*-null sequences in dual spaces”): “Let X be a separable Banach space which is weakly sequentially complete. Does X have property (K)?”
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem from the paper. It has the right hypothesis (X separable and weakly sequentially complete), the right conclusion (property (K)), and it correctly points to the paper’s definition of property (K) in terms of weak*-null sequences in X* having convex block subsequences converging to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X).
missing_details: The paper’s standing convention is that all Banach spaces are real; this ambient assumption is implicit unless stated explicitly.
To make the question fully stand-alone, “weakly sequentially complete” should be defined as: every weakly Cauchy sequence in X converges weakly to a point of X.

The paper explicitly defines a convex block subsequence: y_k^* = sum_{n in I_k} a_n x_n^*, where I_1, I_2, ... are finite subsets of N with max(I_k) < min(I_{k+1}), each a_n >= 0, and sum_{n in I_k} a_n = 1.
The meaning of convergence to 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X*, X) should be unpacked exactly as the paper does: for every weakly compact set K subseteq X, sup_{x in K} |y_k^*(x)| -> 0.
If the question is to be maximally paper-faithful, it should be phrased as an open problem rather than as a broader inquiry about related permanence properties of property (K).
refined_question: Let X be a real separable Banach space that is weakly sequentially complete, meaning that every weakly Cauchy sequence in X converges weakly in X. Must X have property (K); that is, for every weak*-null sequence (x_n^*) in X^*, does there exist a convex block subsequence (y_k^*) of the form y_k^* = sum_{n in I_k} a_n x_n^*, where I_1, I_2, ... are finite subsets of N with max(I_k) < min(I_{k+1}), a_n >= 0, and sum_{n in I_k} a_n = 1 for each k, such that y_k^* -> 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X^*, X)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if X is a real separable weakly sequentially complete Banach space and (x_n^*) is any weak*-null sequence in X^*, must there exist a convex block subsequence (y_k^*) such that for every weakly compact set K subseteq X one has sup_{x in K} |y_k^*(x)| -> 0?
justification: This is exactly Problem 1.9 in the paper, not a neighboring or generalized question. The paragraph immediately preceding Problem 1.9 supplies the paper’s definitions of convex block subsequence and property (K), including the explicit interpretation of μ(X^*, X)-convergence as uniform convergence on weakly compact subsets of X. The only additions needed to make your draft fully stand-alone are the paper’s ambient convention that Banach spaces are real and the standard definition of weak sequential completeness. No broader reformulation is warranted.
